title: "How the Interview Book Will Be Written"
subtitle: "Source-first, concept-first, and ready for spoken practice"
---

# Editorial standards

This guide defines how future book uploads become chapters. It is **not a summary of any book that has not yet been provided**.

## Respect the source

When a source book arrives, begin with its actual title, author, edition, chapter organisation and source limitations. Explain what the book actually covers before proposing a table of contents. Do not substitute a generic interview checklist for the book.

Keep distinct books distinguishable: an original example, a source-derived claim and a practical extension are three different things. Reference the relevant chapter or page wherever the uploaded material supports it.

## Teach the hard idea simply

A strong chapter should answer a hard question through one minimal example instead of a pile of terminology. Work from intuition to abstraction; every mathematical relationship must define all symbols and include concrete numerical substitutions immediately afterwards.

If code is appropriate, write the shortest complete and runnable demonstration that proves the particular point. Use one language or environment at a time; explain when an example is a simplification rather than production-ready engineering.

## Prepare for an interview, not just an exam

A completed chapter may end with a **30-second explanation**, a **two-minute detailed answer**, assumptions that change the solution, and follow-up questions. The spoken version must avoid code reading and must remain understandable when heard aloud.

## Source and correctness checks

Never claim to have read a full textbook when only excerpts were uploaded. Do not reproduce long copyrighted passages or book figures. When multiple texts disagree, describe the disagreement and its assumptions rather than silently combining them. Verify examples using a small test wherever possible.

## Publication workflow

After a book arrives: inspect it, propose/book-map its contents, write actual lessons, add those pages to the Quarto sidebar, run checks and confirm GitHub Pages build status. Avoid publishing folders full of placeholders.
